meetings.name: Searching and Fearless Meeting, workbook study
meetings.formats: 12 Steps Yellow Workbook, Discussion, Loving Parent Guidebook,
meetings.notes: Format is 10 min of introduction, 10 min of reading from workbook (Just started Loving Parent Guidebook as of 4/1/26 after Yellow WB), 10 min of writing on any topic, then sharing until 8:45-8:50, 5-10 min of closing. Update April 2026: THIS MEETING NEEDS SUPPORT FROM THOSE WHO CAN ATTEND REGULARLY AT WEDNESDAY 7:30PM PACIFIC TIME. The meeting was established in the early 2010s, is generally well attended, now mostly by drop ins, with consistently positive feedback from attendees each week. However, only a handful of regulars attend, and regulars share the service roles of Secretary and Serenity keeper (Zoom Host) through a sign up sheet provided at the meeting. If no one signs up, then regulars volunteer for these roles at the start of the meeting. A 10 minute tutorial on how to do these roles takes place at the last meeting of each month. Hope to see you there!

meetings.name: Living Life Meeting
meetings.notes: The Living Life group is a zoom-only meeting of kind folks who share their experiences, hope, and strength in recovering from the effects of dysfunction and addiction. We are diverse in backgrounds, with experiences in alcoholism, food addiction, drug addiction, and codependency. We are also diverse in geography and genders, primarily from across North America, Our meetings last an hour and the first 10 minutes or so are reading from the Big Red Book. The meetings average about 20 people and we strive to keep the focus on ourselves and sharing from our own experiences. We welcome those new to ACA but we don\'t single out newcomers with undue attention. We encourage people to limit their sharing time but we don\'t run a timer. We think of ourselves as welcoming and reassuring each other that recovery is not only possible, it is a wonderful gift worth working. Reach out to the meeting contact for the zoom PW and we normally reply within a few minutes, even at the start of the meeting.

We spend about 30 minutes in breakout rooms (3-5 people) to share our feelings, reflections on the readings, and our recovery journey. This meeting is designed for any ACA member who is interested in healing food and body issues using ACA’s “Solution” of becoming your own ”Loving Parent.” This meeting is not affiliated with ANY 12-Step food recovery program, though many of us participate in those fellowships. All are welcome! This is an OPEN MEETING for those seeking recovery from dysfunction, relationship addiction, and becoming safe, sane, healthy, and whole!

Ссылки на онлайн-собрания (по пятницам и субботам) предоставляет секретарь группы. Для получения ссылки напишите или позвоните по контакту группы. 

Вначале достаточно просто сказать: «Здравствуйте, дайте, пожалуйста, ссылку на собрание ВДА». Ваши личные данные не запрашиваются, анонимность сохраняется.

Мы не даём советов, не оцениваем и не осуждаем. Единственное условие для участия — выздоравливать.

Присоединяйтесь. Мы рады вам.
meetings.instructions:
Каждую  пятницу в 19:00  в онлайн-формате пройдет собрание по изучению 12 Шагов ВДА по желтой тетради.

Вы можете присоединиться к нам из любой точки. 

Важно: задания по шагам выполняются непосредственно на сборе. Вам не нужно готовиться дома. Делиться своими ответами можно по желанию — здесь нет обязанности говорить, если вы не готовы. Мы ценим ваше право на безопасность и комфорт.

Каждую  субботу в 14:00 собираемся онлайн для изучения Путеводителя по Любящему Родителю (доступное на английском языке). Это собрание посвящено развитию внутреннего любящего родителя — навыков, которые помогают нам заботиться о себе здесь и сейчас. Такой же формат предполагает проведение упражнений во время встреч без домашней подготовки.

Каждое  воскресенье в 14:00  мы приглашаем вас на очную встречу по адресу:  Кольцово, 14 (вход со стороны проспекта Академика Сандахчиева напротив парковки). Форма встречи — открытая, читаем литературу ВДА и закрепляем опыт, силу надежды и силы.

meetings.name: Hurting to Healing to Helping
meetings.formats: Discussion, Fellowship Text (BRB), Laundry Lists Workbook, Steps, Traditions,
meetings.notes: We are both at Unity Club (face to face), and also available as a zoom meeting online. Email us for phone call-in or link-in info (emails answered before Sunday meeting up to Saturday 9pm) if you cannot attend in person as we are linking the two together for Hybrid style meeting. We are identified as a Closed style meeting (which means you should not be a reporter or student doing research but rather be looking to experience healing for yourself and/or for your family) -- BUT -- we want to welcome all who believe they may be or are from dysfunctional/shame based homes or alcoholic upbringing etc. Even homes where alcohol was not directly involved satisfy the definition if dysfunction, depression and/or shame is the result in your life. There is no requirement to have literature or even to share at all during our meetings. We use a 3-week cycle of topics: Laundry List (Trait readings from Laundry List Workbook),12 steps (Big Red Book) and then Solution oriented Topics (Inner Child Inner Parent topic in Chapter 8 also in Big Red Book) Please give us a try, we would love to meet you and to welcome you to our fellowship.
meetings.instructions:

meetings.notes:
We do not tolerate emotional disruptions:

Disruptions mean:  

Rudeness including aggression towards others in the meeting

Uncontrolled swearing 

Acting out from our triggered inner family members (child, teen or critic)

Harassment of any kind, including emotional, physical or any financial favors
meetings.instructions:
2 pm Amsterdam Netherlands time (CEST) / 1 PM London time Zoom Id: 835-9004-6441 - Password 711 - English speaking -- Audio only, please do not use your video -- For information, visit acanetherlands.com or FellowWorldTravelers IG728

The exercises and guidance in the Loving Parent Guidebook will help you learn to put your innate qualities of love, compassion, and kindness into action. You will need support from others, and you may need to try things out and make adjustments as you go. Yet, the more you take action coming from love by connecting with your inner family, the more your life will change. You can apply everything you learn in this guidebook to parenting, interacting with children, and interacting with adults. When you become a friend to yourself, you’re naturally a friend to others. Becoming your own loving parent is a process. You may struggle at times and face resistance, but the process is ultimately liberating.

meetings.notes:
LGBTQIAN2S+ is an inclusive acronym representing diverse sexual orientations and gender identities, standing for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer/Questioning, Intersex, Asexual/Aromantic, Non-Binary, Two-Spirit, Plus, encompassing many more identities beyond the initial letters to show full inclusivity for everyone in the community.

"Intragroup" means occurring or existing within a single group, such as a team, or community, contrasting with "intergroup," which involves interactions between different groups. It describes relationships between entities within the same community.

A "semiautonomous part of the whole" refers to a component that has some self-governing abilities, but still depends on the larger system  for essential functions and coordination, forming a partially independent, yet integrated, unit. In broader contexts, it can describe entities (regions, organizations) that manage some affairs but are subject to a larger authority.

i.e. The Unified Expression of the Collective Conscience of the entire Homegroup via Equally Informed & Supported Representation

(HG5+Intragroup Support/Agenda)
meetings.instructions:
Hella Gay ACA(D) is a Home Group for LGBTQIAN2S+AC born into A/D Families/Environments

Go to https://hellagayaca.mailchimpsites.com for login details.

Our Hella Gay Home Group is a unified group of study/workgroup meetings for members of our special interest.

Here, we can feel safer to heal from growing up in a dysfunctional family, and a society where our identities were/are considered inferior.

Listed meetings welcome LGBTQIAN2S+Adult Children of Alcoholics and Dysfunctional Families. 

Closed, signifies closed to the general public, all are designated LGBTQ+ Meeting Focus, as we center the safety of our members.

Study/Workgroups & Committees are supported by the efforts of each meeting's attending Homegroup members.

Each, Hella Gay ACA(D) Homegroup Meeting, is semiautonomous; cooperating with HG5+UIS/ACA, in all matters affecting our Homegroup, or the ACA Fellowship as a whole.

meetings.name: Agnostic ACA Coffee with the Stoics
meetings.notes:
In this Friday meeting, we read from historical writings by Stoic philosophers. We believe that Stoicism has many teachings that support recovery. We do not promote or recommend any book, or wording, over those in ACA literature; instead, we use these writings to support our secular perspective of building healthy experiences in adulthood after growing up in an alcoholic or dysfunctional families.

We are not angry atheists or against a Higher Power. We believe in personal accountability and that ACA recovery can be successful with or without “god.” We acknowledge a Judeo/Christian Higher Power does not work for everyone. If you’d like a secular approach to the 12-steps, we invite you to join us.

AgnosticACA supports the following meetings.  Note that ALL times are USA Eastern Time

This group takes full advantage of the ACA open literature policy. According to this policy Literature policy, “It has always been accepted that ACA groups should remain open in choosing literature. That is, ACA meetings may draw from various sources.”

AgnosticACA is open to everyone in ACA. If you are atheist, agnostic, a freethinker, humanist, uncomfortable with the religious language in ACA literature, questioning what Higher Power means to you, or simply looking for a new meeting, then this group might be for you.

There is only one requirement for ACA membership: the desire to recover from the effects of family dysfunction.

meetings.name: The Voices of the Heart- Sock Puppet Workshop
meetings.notes:
In this hands-on workshop, we use simple sock puppets (without faces) to help show the relationship between two parts of ourselves: the Inner Child and the Loving Parent.

Each person will get a chance to try both roles—speaking as the Inner Child (the part of us that feels angry, fearful, abandoned, loving, joyful, and energized), and also as the Loving Parent (the part that can be kind, caring, supportive, and protective).

Using the sock puppets helps make this inner conversation easier and safer. It gives a little space from big feelings, so we can say things we might keep inside.

This activity helps us learn to talk to ourselves more kindly. Instead of judging or ignoring the Inner Child, the Loving Parent learns to listen, comfort, and care. CLOSED means ACA members only.  We close the room 15 minutes after the workshop starts.

Saturdays: 9 am PT / 12 pm ET / 5 pm UK

Zoom Meeting ID: 818 1504 7514, PW: 519003

Note: Wednesday meetings on an indefinite hiatus due to lack of service.

If you identify as a woman, trans-female or non-binary, you are welcome! We do a reading from Strengthening My Recovery and 5 minutes of journaling to connect with our inner child/teenager. This meeting is based on the assumption that many adult children never learned how to relate to their emotions and bodies in healthy, self-loving ways. We may have a core belief that our bodies are not worthy of love and respect. We may have used disordered eating behaviors to comfort ourselves when our caregivers failed to do so, or to numb our feelings when the pain was unbearable. We help our inner child/teenager understand that these behaviors are not a loving way to relieve their pain and shame. Our feelings are OK—we don’t need to fix them, numb them, or reject them.

meetings.name: ACA and Gifted Global
meetings.notes: This ACA group is for those who identify as gifted, highly talented or creative. If you’re complex, intense, driven and/or highly sensitive, and an adult child, this group may be for you. You may have been told “You’re too much”, “too this” or “too that”; you might have felt like an alien or imposter; or you’ve been burned by your intensity. If so, you might find a home here amongst neurodivergent peers. Gifted people have special needs – especially in childhood. Giftedness can be obscured by ADHD, autism, dyslexia, the effects of family dysfunction and socio-economic factors. People with high IQs exist in every culture around the world; the diversity of this group reflects this.

meetings.name: The Voices of the Heart- Sock Puppet Workshop in JPNS/ ENG
meetings.notes:
In this hands-on workshop, we use simple sock puppets (without faces) to help show the relationship between two parts of ourselves: the Inner Child and the Loving Parent.

Each person will get a chance to try both roles—speaking as the Inner Child (the part of us that feels angry, fearful, abandoned, loving, joyful, and energized), and also as the Loving Parent (the part that can be kind, caring, supportive, and protective).

Using the sock puppets helps make this inner conversation easier and safer. It gives a little space from big feelings, so we can say things we might keep inside.

This activity helps us learn to talk to ourselves more kindly. Instead of judging or ignoring the Inner Child, the Loving Parent learns to listen, comfort, and care. CLOSED means ACA members only. We close the room 15 minutes after the workshop starts.  第1,3,5土曜 (曜日/ 時間設定:アメリカ太平洋岸)は日本語

ACA MABUHAY PHILIPPINES Drop-in Friday- Walang Sala (ACA Identifying Members who may also be Double Winners, part of the LGBTQ Community, and newcomers)

"Walang Sala" is a Tagalog phrase that means "blameless, without sin, or innocent." These are apt words that describe our True Self, our Inner Child. Please come and join our Drop-in Friday meeting where regulars of our Mabuhay Fellowship meet; we will focus on a short meditation, open sharing, and heartfelt declarations of praise/affirmation/gratitude to our Inner Family. We adhere to No-Crosstalk, No-Fixing/Rescuing, No-Predatory Behavior policies; we encourage and invite a gentle and safe healing space for all attendees.

meetings.name: Life of Love: Living a Spiritually Sustainable Lifestyle
meetings.formats: 12 Steps Yellow Workbook, Discussion, Laundry Lists Workbook, Loving Parent Guidebook, Speaker, Steps,
meetings.notes:
This is a non-traditional ACA meeting dedicated to nurturing a spiritually sustainable recovery lifestyle. Each month, we explore an ACA recovery topic in combination with an external practice or tool—such as somatic work, creative expression, spiritual rituals, trauma-informed care, diet, plant-based healing, and other lifestyle practices.

We ground our shares in ACA principles and literature while welcoming personal experience with outside tools. This meeting is inclusive of members in multi-program recovery who draw from a range of practices to heal, regulate, and grow.

Our format includes conference approved literature readings, workshop questions, brief meditations/reflections, and open sharing. We also host a monthly speaker meeting. Members are encouraged to share from their personal experience and avoid giving advice or prescribing tools.

This meeting uses both conference-approved and non-conference-approved content to support deeper reflection and sustainable daily routines. We respect the diversity of recovery paths and hold space for the unfolding of each person’s healing journey with humility, curiosity, and care.

meetings.name: Book Group Study for Women Incest Survivors: "The Picture of Health"
meetings.notes:
We are a book group beginning study of “The Picture of Health”. The group is still open to newcomers. 

We begin our first art exercise within the first minute of the meeting, so you will miss that if you are late. We then read and do more exercises from the book, and then have time for sharing. There is no "homework" between meetings. We go through the book together all at one slow pace. No need to "catch up" before you join.

This group is open to women who know or suspect she is a survivor of childhood incest. While we hold a deep respect for our transgender friends, this group is only open to adult women who were girls as children. 

Some basic art supplies are required however, if you’re dropping in for the first time, any pencil, pen, crayon, or creative improvising will do. Meetings consist of reading, creating, and timed shares.

meetings.name: Healing through Art
meetings.formats: Discussion, Fellowship Text (BRB), Loving Parent Guidebook, Strengthening My Recovery, Workshop,
meetings.notes:
This ACA meeting integrates recovery and creative expression. Each meeting begins with a short reading from ACA literature (Big Red Book, Loving Parent Guidebook, or Strengthening My Recovery). Participants are then invited to spend about 15 minutes  responding to the reading through creative expression using a medium of their choice, such as drawing, writing, poetry, music, or journaling.

Members may share their creation and reflect on what came up for them. The meeting then continues with open ACA sharing related to recovery. This is not about performance or perfection; creativity is simply used as a gentle way to connect with our inner family and authentic selves. Sharing artwork is always optional, and no artistic experience is required.
meetings.instructions: Please email acahealingthruart@gmail.com for Zoom ID and password.

Weekly Socks Full of Love Puppet Workshop –

email for password contact- Terry at: Socksfulloflove@gmail.com

Women Only – Closed  (English)

This unique and heartfelt workshop invites Adult Children into a space of creative healing using something as simple—and powerful—as socks. Together, we create hand puppets that represent two deeply important parts of ourselves: our Inner Child and our Loving Parent.

Through guided prompts and gentle structure, participants use these puppets to explore internal dialogues—giving voice to the Inner Child’s needs, feelings, fears, and joys, while also learning to respond from the Loving Parent part of themselves with compassion, protection, and understanding.
